title: Absolute moment of a Gaussian linear form
statement:
For $n\ge 0$ and coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$ have independent standard Gaussian coordinates. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}\left|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i Z_i\right|\,d\gamma_n(Z)=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2}\,2\varphi(0),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density on $\mathbb R$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is a real coefficient for each of the $n$ coordinates
replaced: For every $n\ge0$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$, if $Z$ is a standard Gaussian vector and $\varphi$ is the one-dimensional standard Gaussian density, then $\mathbb E|\sum_i a_i Z_i|=\sqrt{\sum_i a_i^2}\,2\varphi(0)$.
